English-Language Proficiency Requirements
Effective for applications submitted for Spring 2027 and later terms only.
The ability to communicate effectively in English — to read, write and speak the language fluently — is vital to your success as a USC student.
International graduate applicants are therefore expected to demonstrate their proficiency in English as part of the application process and should carefully review the guidelines below.
U.S. citizens and legal permanent residents (green card holders) are considered to be “domestic” applicants, regardless of where they have studied or reside. Domestic applicants are exempt from the university’s English-proficiency requirements.
Back to Top
Test Score Guidelines
Important: USC does not set university-wide score minimums for graduate admission. The scores listed below are typically used for placement purposes only — to determine if an admitted student will need to take the International Student English (ISE) examination upon arrival at USC.
English-proficiency scores must be dated within 2 years (24 months) of the date you submit your graduate application. For example, a prospective student applying to fall 2027 who submits their USC application in December 2026 will need to have taken the test no earlier than December 2024.
Please also note that USC does not accept “superscoring”, i.e., combining the highest section scores from multiple test dates (EX: TOEFL MyBestScores, IELTS One-Skill Retake). In order to waive the English-proficiency requirement, all subscores must come from the same test sitting.
Back to Top
TOEFL (Test of English as a Foreign Language)
USC accepts the TOEFL iBT Home Edition, iBT Paper Edition, and the standard in-person TOEFL iBT administered in official test centers. Admitted students are exempt from taking the ISE Exam with the following scores:*
For exams taken prior to January 21, 2026:
PhD programs
100 or above, with 20 or above in each section.
Master’s degree programs
90 or above, with 20 or above in each section.
For exams taken on or after January 21, 2026:
PhD programs
5 or above, with 4 or above in each section.
Master’s degree programs
4.5 or above, with 4 or above in each section.
*As of January 21, 2026, ETS uses an updated scoring system for the TOEFL.
Sending official scores to USC: USC must receive scores electronically from the testing service for them to be considered official. Photocopies or paper copies of scores are not acceptable.
USC’s institution code is 4852. No department code is required.
Back to Top
IELTS (International English Language Testing System)
USC accepts IELTS Academic and IELTS Online scores. Admitted students are exempt from taking the ISE Exam with the following scores:
PhD programs
7 or above, with 6 or above on each band.
Master’s degree programs
6.5 or above, with 6 or above on each band.
Sending official scores to USC:
Select “University of Southern California — Graduate Admission” from the list of available institutions when you register to take the IELTS test. Alternatively, provide this information to your testing center after you have taken the test. Contact information for the USC department to which you are applying is not required.
USC must receive scores electronically from the testing service for them to be considered official. Photocopies or paper copies of scores from the testing service are not acceptable.
Back to Top
Cambridge English Qualifications
USC accepts the Cambridge English C1 Advanced Exam. Admitted students are exempt from taking the ISE Exam with the following scores:
PhD programs
185 or above, with 169 or above on each skill.
Master’s degree programs
176 or above, with 169 or above on each skill.
Sending official scores to USC:
Select “University of Southern California” from the list of available institutions when you register to take the C1 Advanced Exam. Alternatively, provide this information to your testing center after you have taken the test. Contact information for the USC department to which you are applying is not required.
USC must receive scores electronically from the testing service for them to be considered official. Photocopies or paper copies of scores from the testing service are not acceptable.
Back to Top
PTE (Pearson Test of English) Academic
USC accepts PTE Academic and PTE Academic Online scores. Admitted students are exempt from taking the ISE Exam with the following scores:
PhD programs
68 or above, with 53 or above on each band.
Master’s degree programs
61 or above, with 53 or above on each band.
Sending official scores to USC:
Select “University of Southern California” from the list of available institutions when you register to take the PTE Academic test. Alternatively, provide this information to your testing center after you have taken the test. Contact information for the USC department to which you are applying is not required.
USC must receive scores electronically from the testing service for them to be considered official. Photocopies or paper copies of scores from the testing service are not acceptable.
Back to Top
Special Accommodations
The Educational Testing Service (TOEFL), the British Council (IELTS), Pearson (PTE Academic) and Cambridge English (C1 Advanced Exam) will provide accommodations for those with disabilities.
Back to Top
Score Minimums Set by Programs
Please note that some individual programs may set internal score minimums that are higher than those listed here. Please refer to your intended graduate program(s) for information about their English proficiency requirements.
Back to Top
English-Language Test Waiver
International applicants are exempt from submitting English-proficiency scores under the following circumstances:
You hold a degree (bachelor’s, master’s, or doctorate) from USC or are currently enrolled in a USC degree program.
You hold a bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited university in the United States or the equivalent of a U.S. bachelor’s degree from an officially recognized university in another qualifying Anglophone country where English is both the only official language and the language of instruction.
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎
To determine degree equivalency, please refer to our country requirements.
‎ ‎ ‎
Students who transferred credits from a non-Anglophone country may still qualify for this waiver if they subsequently completed their bachelor’s degree in the United States or another qualifying Anglophone country. The bachelor’s degree does not need to have been completed entirely in the qualifying country.
‎ ‎
Dual-degree holders who completed only part of their degree in the U.S. or another qualifying country do not qualify for this waiver.
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎
You have completed a master’s or doctoral degree from a country in which English is both the language of instruction and the only official language. The degree needs to have already been completed at the time you submit your USC application. Applicants who have not yet completed a qualifying master’s or doctoral program at the time they apply will still need to submit English-proficiency scores.
Your native language is English. This applies to native English speakers from countries such as the United Kingdom, Australia, New Zealand, and Canada (except Quebec), where English is both the only official language of the country and the language of instruction.
USC does not waive the English-proficiency requirement based on any other consideration such as work experience, ESL enrollment, amount of time spent in the U.S., etc. It also cannot be waived on the basis of programs taught in English in non-Anglophone countries.
To determine if USC requires TOEFL/IELTS/PTE scores for your country of study, please check our Country Requirements page.
Back to Top
USC International Academy
Students looking to prepare their English and academic skills for the rigors of graduate study at USC may wish to explore the USC International Academy as an option.
Exceptions: The Office of Graduate Admission does not have the authority to grant exemptions to the university’s English-proficiency policies on the basis of applicant requests. Exemption requests submitted directly to our office by applicants themselves are automatically denied. If you have extraordinary circumstances that you believe may merit an individualized exemption, please contact your intended graduate program to discuss available options.

The University of Southern California’s Annual Security and Fire Safety Report (ASR) is now available online at: https://dps.usc.edu/alerts/annual-report/.
The Annual Security and Fire Safety Report includes Clery Act crime and fire statistics for locations owned and/or controlled by USC, the required policy disclosure statements and other important safety related information. A paper copy of the ASR is available on request made to Department of Public Safety Records by calling (213) 740-6000, by email to DPSRecords@dps.usc.edu or in person at DPS at 3667 South McClintock Avenue, Los Angeles, California 90089.
